parallels.scholarly_caveat: Aphrodite also has Indo-European elements (daughter of Zeus, dawn-goddess traits); the derivation is partial.

basis: The Pyrgi tablets dedicate one temple in Etruscan to Uni and in Phoenician to Astarte
Same donor, same sanctuary, c. 500 BCE
Feminine and masculine forms of the same Semitic Venus-star deity name (ʿṯtrt / ʿṯtr)
Both personify the Venus star
South Arabia kept the male form, the Levant the female
Berossus says Artaxerxes II was the first to set up statues of Aphrodite Anaitis in Babylon, Susa and Ecbatana
Anahita's royal cult image drew on Mesopotamian Ishtar iconography
Both are invoked by kings for victory
primary_text_evidence: Berossus via Clement of Alexandria, Protrepticus 5
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Anahita's Avestan core (the heavenly river) is Indo-Iranian; the Ishtar features are a later Achaemenid layer.

basis: Armenian Anahit is the Iranian Anahita adopted with Zoroastrian-influenced religion
Strabo records the cult of Anaitis in Armenian Acilisene
Same name and role as mother and protectress
Both are a sacred heavenly river personified as goddess
Both purify and give fertility
Avestan Harahvaiti is the cognate of Sarasvati as a river name, and Anahita's river shares her attributes
The trilingual inscription of Pauli Gerrei names the same god as Eshmun (Punic), Asklepios (Greek) and Aesculapius (Latin)
Both are healing gods with serpents and incubation shrines
A beautiful youth castrates himself to escape the desire of a great goddess
He dies and is restored or made immortal by her
Both are worshipped as dying-and-revived gods
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Eshmun's story survives only in Damascius and may be shaped by the Attis myth.

basis: Roman African dedications call the god of the former tophets Saturnus
Greek authors call Baal Hammon Kronos
Both are the old enthroned father-god of grain and harvest
Aged enthroned father of the gods
Philo of Byblos identifies El with Kronos, as Baal Hammon was identified with Kronos
Sphinx/cherub throne iconography
Punic tophet stelae record mlk offerings to Baal Hammon
The Hebrew Bible places Molek's rite at a tophet
Both involve dedications of children by fire
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Whether mlk names a god or a type of offering, and whether the tophets held sacrifices or burials, are both debated.

basis: The Idalion bilingual equates Resheph with Apollo (Resheph-mkl = Apollo Amyklos)
Both shoot arrows of plague
Both can avert the plague they send
Ugaritic equivalence lists match Resheph with Nergal
Both are gods of plague, war and the underworld gate
Philo of Byblos identifies Chousor with Hephaestus
Both are the smith of the gods who forges weapons and builds palaces for the high gods
primary_text_evidence: Philo of Byblos, Phoenician History (via Eusebius, Praeparatio Evangelica 1.10)

basis: Ugaritic texts place Kothar's seat at Hkpt (Memphis), Ptah's city
Both are divine patrons of craftsmen and builders
The sun passes through the underworld each night
The sun deity therefore mediates between the living and the dead
Both rise renewed at dawn
Female sun deity
Travels across the sky by day and through or under the earth by night
Deity of grain and the harvest
Philo of Byblos renders Dagon as Siton, 'grain'
National god whose anger lets enemies oppress his people and whose favour restores them
Captured towns devoted to him (ḥrm / herem)
Judges 11:24 sets Chemosh and Yahweh side by side as givers of land
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Structural parallel only; the Mesha Stele's theology closely resembles Deuteronomistic language.

basis: Both names derive from mlk 'king'
The Hebrew Bible sometimes confuses them (1 Kings 11:7 vs 11:5)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Milcom is the Ammonite national god; Molek is associated with the Hinnom rite. Identification is not established.

basis: National god of an Iron Age kingdom
The people described as his children / his people
Royal works and treaties dedicated to him
The name ʿAtarʿateh combines ʿAthtar (Astarte) with ʿAttah (Anat)
Great goddess of a Syrian city with Astarte's roles
Great mother enthroned between lions
Served by eunuch galli priests in ecstatic rites
Lucian notes the resemblance to Rhea
Palmyrene–Greek bilingual inscriptions render Baalshamin as Zeus
Both are lords of heaven and rain
Storm and heaven god called Baal
Giver of rain and kingship
At Palmyra Allat's temple housed a Greek-style Athena statue
Palmyrene inscriptions equate Allat with Athena
Warrior-protectress of her sanctuary and people
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Herodotus instead equated Alilat with Aphrodite Ourania; identifications varied by region.

basis: Venus-star goddess
Invoked for protection and in war
Worshipped with sacred trees and stones
Personifies the apportioned share of life
Governs the hour of death
Name from a root meaning 'to apportion' (mny), as moira means 'portion'
Goddess who decrees human fate
Fate as allotment
Major oracle by casting or drawing lots (arrows at Mecca, oak lots at Praeneste)
The lot reveals the god's decision on practical matters
National god sometimes understood as lunar
Protector of the people
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Wadd's lunar identity is uncertain.

basis: Greek writers identified Dusares with Dionysus
Vine imagery in Nabataean and Hauran sanctuaries
Epiphanius describes a birth festival of Dusares like that of a divine child
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Dushara was also equated with Zeus; the Dionysus identification may reflect festal and vine aspects only.

basis: Both worshipped in the form of an aniconic black stone
The stone itself is the god's throne or presence
Same Indo-Iranian god *Mitra, 'covenant'
Both guard contracts and friendship
Both invoked in the Mitanni treaty c. 1380 BCE
Roman Mithras bears the name of the Iranian yazata
Both are associated with the sun and with contract (Mithras shakes hands with Sol)
Roman authors present the cult as Persian
parallels.scholarly_caveat: How much of Roman Mithraism derives from Iranian Mithra cult, versus being a new Roman creation, is strongly debated.

basis: All-seeing guarantor of oaths and justice
Associated with the sun
